The two Go caches are the issue's, not each role's: /legion/go/build and /legion/go/mod, as UV_CACHE_DIR already was. The architect asked for it after the reviewer raised it, and is correcting the specification's acceptance line himself (no two roles told one scratch directory). What stays per role is what needs isolation: bun's install cache, because bun hardlinks out of it into whatever it installs for, and the state home, because Oh My Pi's browser broker lock is an abstract unix socket named from a path under it, one name across every container of the pod — plus the temporary directory and the cache and data homes. The claim made about the documentation is exactly this and no more: `go help cache` says the build cache is safe for concurrent invocations of the go command, and the module cache holds content verified against a known hash in a directory the go command makes read-only; the live two-at-once build is what carries the module cache.

The per-role bun cache was justified by 'one cache shared between two roles' checkouts': workspace.Location names the repository and the issue, never a role, so all six roles work one clone and one node_modules — a file edited in place there is already in the packages every role runs from, and what a cache per role confines is afterwards, only that role's later installs putting the changed copy back. Decision block 964174d5 on the specification carries the human-facing half, corrected by the architect; these comments say the same thing in the code's own words and reopen nothing.
